text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Under a government energy programme for winter, Romanian refineries are to process 550,000 tonnes of crude from domestic production and 800,000 tonnes of imported oil per month to secure fuel oil demand.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Only 650 billion lei of an allotted 1.1 trillion to fund the wheat and barley harvest have actually reached farmers, the newspaper quotes the Agriculture Ministry as saying.
- Roman SA truck maker is expected soon to sign a cooperation accord with U.S. truck manufacturer Novistar International.
LIBERTATEA
- Investment funds in Romania saw their units rise by 0.01 to 7.22 percent last month.
General:
ROMANIA LIEBRA

- The "Reporters sans Frontieres" organisation asked President Ion Iliescu to stop putting pressure on a Romanian journalist who helped uncover fake telephone polls allegedly commissioned by the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR).
- The newspaper publishes the list of candidates of the main opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc in the November 3 general election.
ADEVARUL
- An editorial wonders in whose interest confusion is being sown among voters by the government and the ruling PDSR ahead of the November 3 presidential and parliamentary election.
- As many as 63,500 tenants have requested to buy the flats they live in, but only those not claimed by their former owners can be sold now.
- The upper house, the Senate, approved a decree under which Romanians will cast ballots in the November polls only by producing their identity documents.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The newspaper publishes a report by the Italian prosecutor's office saying that a Romanian minister whose identity is not disclosed is involved in the illegal trafficking of guns between Romania and Italy.
- Wim van Velzen, president of the Christian Democratic European Union allegedly said that Romania will not be admitted to the EU if President Iliescu wins the polls.
- President Iliescu orders accreditation withdrawn from photographers after the leading daily Adevarul published a picture of him adressing workers from behind a wire fence.

- The newspaper prints a full-page report on the so-called "Peregrines" operation of the former Securitate secret police under which the emigration right of Romanians and Jews had been sold for millions of dollars in the communist era.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Eugen Vasiliu, chief prosecutor of the penal investigation department says he does not know why he was sacked last Friday.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The newspaper publishes a two-page interview with Romania's former King Michael, living in exile in the Swiss town of Versoix.
LIBERTATEA
- Romanian women have no recourse over sexual harassment, says judge Arline Praht. The next parliament must adopt a law to protect women against such offences.
ZIUA

- Some 300,000 votes could be altered in the November polls as ballot papers for Romanians living abroad will be transported by the Tarom SA state airline without any proper security measures, said Adrian Dumitrescu, head of the December 21 association of "revolutionaries".

- Constantin Ticu Dumitrescu, head of the Senate's commission watching over fraud says President Iliescu's election campaign is financed by the "financial mafia". ($=3,262 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
